ms.feature.name: Market shocks
ms.feature.desc: Fab incidents, memory and wafer price spikes, booms and recessions
ms.settings.intensity.tooltip: How strong the shocks are: ×0.5 "Mild", ×1 "Normal", ×1.5 "Harsh", ×2 "Chaos". Deviations of multipliers and sums of money are scaled, but the multipliers never leave the limits of the pack. Shocks already under way do not change.
ms.settings.title: Settings: market shocks
ms.settings.frequency.tooltip: How often random shocks fire: ×0.5 rarer, ×1 normal, ×1.5 more often. The memory price and demand cycles run regardless of the frequency.
ms.fx.ramp: {0}: up to {1} (rise {2} d, peak {3} d, fall {4} d), until {5}
ms.fx.forecast_missed: The forecast did not come true
ms.fab_fire.title: Fire at {0}'s fab
ms.fab_fire.text: A fire broke out at the fab of {0}: some of the lines are stopped until the repair is done. Output will drop, and the cost of the repair falls on the company. Warning: contract shortfalls are fined.
ms.fab_fire.cause: More lines mean more risk: the chance of an incident at {0} is proportional to its share of world fab capacity.
ms.cleanroom_contamination.title: Cleanroom contamination at {0}
ms.cleanroom_contamination.text: Dust got into the cleanrooms of the fab of {0}: part of the finished processors in the warehouse is written off as scrap, and the defect rate will rise over the next weeks.
ms.cleanroom_contamination.cause: More lines mean more risk: the chance of an incident at {0} is proportional to its share of world fab capacity.
ms.grid_failure.title: Power grid failure at {0}
ms.grid_failure.text: A failure of the power grid has idled the fab of {0}, and restarting the equipment makes the work dearer. Warning: contract shortfalls are fined.
ms.grid_failure.cause: More lines mean more risk: the chance of an incident at {0} is proportional to its share of world fab capacity.
ms.litho_breakdown.title: Lithography tool breakdown at {0}
ms.litho_breakdown.text: A lithography tool at the fab of {0} has broken down. You can rent equipment to get the output back sooner, or wait for the repair. Warning: contract shortfalls are fined.
ms.litho_breakdown.cause: More lines mean more risk: the chance of an incident at {0} is proportional to its share of world fab capacity.
ms.earthquake.title: Earthquake in the fab regions
ms.earthquake.text: An earthquake has stopped fabs across the industry: output is down, repairs are needed, and memory gets dearer while suppliers rebuild their lines. Warning: contract shortfalls are fined.
ms.earthquake.cause: A rare industry-wide accident: the fabs sit in a few seismic regions, so the blow lands on all of them at once.
ms.photoresist_shortage.title: Photoresist shortage
ms.photoresist_shortage.text: Photoresist suppliers cannot keep up with demand: fabs run in fits and starts, and materials get dearer. Warning: contract shortfalls are fined.
ms.photoresist_shortage.cause: Only a handful of suppliers make photoresist, so a failure at one of them hits the whole industry.
ms.logistics_crunch.title: Logistics crunch
ms.logistics_crunch.text: Shipments of materials are stuck in ports and warehouses, and delivery gets dearer for everyone who sells processors.
ms.logistics_crunch.cause: Supply chains stretch around the world: a delay in one link shows up in the unit cost of every company.
ms.dram_spike_warning.title: Analysts: memory prices are about to rise
ms.dram_spike_warning.text: Analysts warn of a coming jump in memory prices. You can stock up on memory now or wait, but a forecast does not always come true.
ms.dram_spike_warning.cause: Memory suppliers are cutting output while stocks on the market run down.
ms.dram_spike.title: Memory price spike
ms.dram_spike.text: Memory has got dearer: the more cache a processor has, the more its unit cost grows. Prices will be back to normal only after several months.
ms.dram_spike.cause: Demand for memory has outrun the output of the suppliers' plants.
ms.dram_glut.title: Memory glut
ms.dram_glut.text: Memory is getting cheaper: the market is oversupplied, and the unit cost of processors with a big cache falls.
ms.dram_glut.cause: Suppliers have raised memory output faster than demand has grown.
ms.wafer_shortage.title: Silicon wafer shortage
ms.wafer_shortage.text: There are not enough silicon wafers and they are getting dearer: the material costs more in production for everyone who makes processors.
ms.wafer_shortage.cause: Silicon capacity is fully booked, and there are more orders than wafers.
ms.energy_crisis.title: Energy crisis
ms.energy_crisis.text: Electricity is getting dearer, and the running costs of fabs go up for every company.
ms.energy_crisis.cause: Fuel shortages have pushed up energy rates for industry.
ms.memory_cycle.title: Memory price cycle
ms.memory_cycle.text: Memory prices have started a wave: they rise and fall with a period of about four years. The wave begins and ends at the normal level, with no jumps.
ms.memory_cycle.cause: Memory makers keep expanding and cutting capacity as demand goes.
ms.recession_warning.title: Analysts: expect a recession
ms.recession_warning.text: Analysts forecast a fall in demand. You can cut costs ahead of time (fabs get cheaper to run, but research slows down) or stay the course. A forecast does not always come true.
ms.recession_warning.cause: The economy is slowing down and buyers are putting off buying computers.
ms.recession.title: Recession
ms.recession.text: Demand for processors has fallen in every segment, most of all for the most expensive ones. Warehouses will fill up: review your prices and your production plan.
ms.recession.cause: An economic downturn: buyers are putting off upgrading their equipment.
ms.pc_boom.title: Personal computer boom
ms.pc_boom.text: Demand for mid-range and budget processors is growing: computers are entering every home and office.
ms.pc_boom.cause: Computers have got cheaper and the mass buyer has come to the market.
ms.server_boom.title: Server boom
ms.server_boom.text: Demand for the most powerful processors is growing: companies are building server capacity en masse.
ms.server_boom.cause: Businesses are moving their data and services onto networks and data centers.
ms.embedded_boom.title: Embedded systems boom
ms.embedded_boom.text: Demand for industrial and embedded processors is growing: electronics are appearing in appliances, cars and machine tools.
ms.embedded_boom.cause: Equipment makers are replacing mechanics with electronics.
ms.silicon_cycle.title: A new silicon cycle
ms.silicon_cycle.text: Demand for processors has started a wave with a period of about five years: upswing and downswing follow each other smoothly, in every segment at once.
ms.silicon_cycle.cause: The industry lives in cycles: a glut of capacity gives way to a shortage, and back again.
ms.dumping_complaint.title: Anti-dumping complaint against {0}
ms.dumping_complaint.text: Competitors have accused {0} of selling processors below cost. You can accept the duty or spend money on lobbying, which does not guarantee success.
ms.dumping_complaint.cause: A processor sells for less than its real unit cost, and the market share of {0} is noticeable.
ms.launch_hype.title: Buzz around a new processor from {0}
ms.launch_hype.text: A fresh processor from {0} is in the spotlight of the press and the buyers: interest in it is growing.
ms.launch_hype.cause: {0} has a new processor, and the chance of a buzz is proportional to its market share.
